fields.currentSituation: The map-making experience, including the Detail Drawer, is implemented entirely in React with direct drawlib integrations.
fields.desiredOutcome: Migrate bounded map-making slices to Angular while preserving observable behavior, starting with the LineForm Length/Angle/Fence offset editing flow.
fields.whyMatters: A bounded migration reduces integration risk and produces reusable migration evidence for the remaining Detail Drawer forms.
successCriteria: The approved Detail Drawer LineForm slice preserves its agreed scenarios.
React retains the drawer shell, shared inputs/radio components and canvas ownership during this slice.
fields.richReleaseNotes: The Detail Drawer LineForm slice (Length, Angle, Fence offset selector and distance) passed independent verification: all 7 contract scenarios and all 4 visual parity surfaces passed in the Route Assistant desktop application (Juno Flex robot for the FeedPush-gated controls, Brownies for confirming they are absent). The broader Map Making Page migration continues with the next bounded slice still to be selected; the Targetprocess items for this Story and its Tasks still need to be applied.

fields.userValue: As a map editor, I want to edit Length, Angle and, where available, Fence offset of the line I have selected or am drawing, and close with Done, so the map updates without losing existing behavior.
fields.currentBehavior: Angular owns the Length, Angle and Fence offset (selector plus distance value) fields, mounted inside the retained React LineForm.tsx via createApplication()/createComponent(); LineForm.tsx keeps owning the Selected Line label, LineRiskCard, Detectable section, Coordinates/Distances, Done button and delete button. This has now passed independent verification.
fields.desiredBehavior: All 7 declared scenarios and all 4 declared visual parity surfaces pass independent verification and the required manual Route Assistant desktop validation, which they now do.
acceptanceCriteria: The drawer shows the selected line's Length and Angle, and its Fence offset when the active robot has the FeedPush capability.
Valid edits update the SVG line and preserve undo/redo exactly as today, including the key-press-gated history rule for Length and Angle.
An empty, non-numeric, zero-length or unchanged value is silently ignored, matching today's guards.
Fence offset controls are fully absent when the active robot lacks the FeedPush capability.
Closing with the retained Done button and reopening does not retain stale state or duplicate listeners.
attentionPoints: FocusNumberInput.tsx's near-zero-value hiding behavior while a line is actively being drawn is not reproduced in the Angular fields; this is a disclosed, out-of-scope gap (migration-result.limitations) not tied to any declared scenario, confirmed still present during manual validation.
The Fence offset distance field's onBlur also invokes restoreLengthIfInvalid, matching LineForm.tsx's existing wiring on both fields; manually confirmed as expected (not a regression).
The baseline and implementation Targetprocess items still need to be applied manually; this handoff does not assume they were.
No push was performed or required for this flow (checkpointPolicy.pushPolicy is 'never').
fields.attachmentInformation: Attach the validated verification-result.json reference; do not attach source copies.
fields.richReleaseNotes: Length, Angle and Fence offset (selector + distance) passed independent verification: targeted test/typecheck/build all pass, and all 7 scenarios plus all 4 visual parity surfaces were manually confirmed in the Route Assistant desktop application against a real selected line, using the Juno Flex robot (has FeedPush) and Brownies (lacks FeedPush).
